claims.claim: #2: When one of several clips fails to read its sound and the rest are fine, the Export-ready card still says 'Sound ✓', and the warning lines are gone or hidden by then.
claims.evidence: js/exporter.js:736-751: the partial message ('N clips had no usable audio — the rest are in the file', :739) goes only to exportSay and a toast. FM._audioTrackDropped is set only `if (!any)` (:748). The run hands over `hasAudio: !!mix, audioDropped: FM._audioTrackDropped || null` (:1620). js/app.js:6247 hides #export-overlay before the card opens, and that overlay is the element holding the amber #export-note line (index.html:798 and :814). The toast also sits behind the overlay (app.js:6263-6269). The card then reaches `out.hasAudio ? 'Sound ✓'` (app.js:6280-6282), and #export-ready (index.html:830-840) has nowhere else for the warning to appear. The only record that survives is the 'drops' line in the localStorage report (exporter.js:1584). Claim #3's out-of-memory decode failures go into the same `dropped` list, so they end in this same 'Sound ✓'.
claims.user_impact: A project with a song plus a clip whose sound could not be read exports with part of its audio missing, and the last screen tells him 'Sound ✓'.
claims.smallest_fix: At exporter.js:1620, add `audioMissing: mix ? (FM._lastAudioDrops || []).length : 0`. That list is already reset at the start of every run (:1213). At app.js:6281, show 'Sound — N clip(s) missing' when audioMissing > 0, and set the xr-nosound class at :6288 for that case too. Add one test: one good clip plus one clip that fails to decode, and the card text and class are asserted.

claims.claim: #3: A big source file can be too large to decode on a phone. The export reads the whole file into memory to get its sound, which can fail or crash the tab.
claims.evidence: Code path confirmed. exporter.js:562 calls `FM.decodeAudio(m.file)` with no options (full sample rate) and no size check. media.js:833-850 runs `await file.arrayBuffer()` on the whole file, so a 1 GB 4K video means 1 GB in RAM before decoding starts, and every error is caught and returned as null. That makes the exporter's own catch at :563 effectively dead, and the 'out of memory' reason is lost. Three other paths that decode a file refuse above 300 MB 'not worth the risk of losing the tab': the waveform (media.js:260, :913-917), the audio probe (media.js:955) and Extract Audio on import (app.js:5457-5461). The export path skips that ceiling. The decoded sound is also kept on the record (exporter.js:562) until the record is released (media.js:60), so it stays in memory after the export. The mix is built before any video frame (exporter.js:1276, muxer at :1373), so a tab kill here happens before crash-resume has saved anything. Not verified: the real memory limit on his iPhone. The audit's suggested fix (decode at the 8 kHz probe rate) would wreck export sound quality and should not be used.
claims.user_impact: Exporting a long 4K iPhone clip can crash the app at the start of the export, or quietly drop that clip's sound, which then shows as 'Sound ✓' because of claim #2.
claims.smallest_fix: At exporter.js:561, before decoding, check whether m.file.size is over FM.media.WAVE_MAX_BYTES on a phone. If it is, add the clip to `dropped` with its own reason ('too big to read its sound on this device') instead of risking the tab. After the export, set m.audioBuffer back to undefined so the decoded sound is not kept in memory. The proper fix later is to read only the audio track: FM.soundTrackInFile already walks the moov box.

claims.claim: #4: If the browser's AAC encoder leaves out decoderConfig.description, the MP4 gets an unplayable audio track while the card says 'Sound ✓' and the report says TRACK WRITTEN. The audit's fix: treat a missing description as encode-failed.
claims.evidence: Both exporter muxers are built with `audio: { codec: 'aac', ... }` (exporter.js:1376, and :1100 for M4A). With codec 'aac', vendor/mp4-muxer.js:1639-1653 fills in decoderConfig.description at construction with its own AAC-LC config, built from the sample rate and channel count. Encoder metadata is only merged on top (mp4-muxer.js:1683-1688, `Object.assign(track.info.decoderConfig, meta.decoderConfig)`). A browser that leaves out the description therefore does not blank it, and esds (mp4-muxer.js:536-566) is written from the built-in config, which matches what the encoder was set up with (mp4a.40.2, exporter.js:950). dropPriming (exporter.js:909, :920) only moves the encoder's config onto the first frame kept. Remaining risk: an encoder that supplies a zero-length description would overwrite the built-in config. No spec-following AAC encoder should do that.
claims.user_impact: No silent-export bug here today, but the audit's suggested check would turn exports that currently play with sound into video-only files on any browser that leaves out the description.
claims.smallest_fix: None needed. Do not apply the audit's 'missing description means encode-failed' check. If a guard is wanted, refuse only a description that is present and has byteLength 0.

claims.claim: #8: Audio-only export (WAV/M4A) saves with a plain link click after the mix and encode have finished, with no share sheet and no Save tap, so iOS may drop the file while the toast says 'Audio exported'.
claims.evidence: Code confirmed. app.js:5962 waits for buildAudioMix and :5982 waits for encodeM4A (both can take seconds), then app.js:6001-6003 does `a.click()` on a blob URL with no fresh tap from him and revokes the URL after 1000 ms. The MP4 fallback waits 4000 ms (exporter.js:52). app.js:6004 shows 'Audio exported — Ns' no matter what happened. The MP4 path waits for a fresh tap: the card's Save button (app.js:6243-6247 onward, index.html:824-838) explains it exists because share() needs that tap. deliver() (exporter.js:66-75) hard-codes type 'video/mp4' at :68, so audio cannot reuse it unchanged. Not verified: whether iOS Safari, especially the installed home-screen app, really drops a download that no tap started. That needs a real iPhone.
claims.user_impact: On an iPhone, 'Export audio' can say 'Audio exported' while no file appears anywhere.
claims.smallest_fix: Send the audio blob through the existing showExportReady card so Save is a fresh tap. Give deliver() a type parameter (audio/wav or audio/mp4) so the share sheet can open. As a quick stopgap, raise the revoke delay at app.js:6003 to 4000 ms to match exporter.js:52.

export-no-sound.summary:
Checked four claims from the audit against b46b47d3, reading code only (no tests, no browser).

1. Confirmed: one clip that fails to read its sound still gives a 'Sound ✓' card (exporter.js:748 sets the flag only when every clip fails; app.js:6247 hides the overlay holding the amber warning before the card opens). This is a real 'my sound is missing but the app said it was fine' path.

2. Partly confirmed: the export reads each source file whole into memory (exporter.js:562 → media.js:836). Three other places in the app refuse files over 300 MB because of tab crashes, and the export skips that limit. The real iPhone memory limit is not verified, and the audit's 8 kHz fix would ruin export sound quality.

3. Wrong: the 'missing encoder description makes an unplayable track' claim. The bundled muxer fills in its own AAC config for codec 'aac' (vendor/mp4-muxer.js:1639-1653) and only merges what the encoder supplies on top (:1683-1688). The audit's proposed fix would cause silent exports rather than prevent them.

4. Partly confirmed: audio-only export saves with a link click after the work finishes, with no Save tap, revokes the file URL after 1 s, and always shows 'Audio exported' (app.js:6001-6004). Whether iOS really drops the file needs a real iPhone.

Highest-value fix: pass the partial-drop count to the ready card (exporter.js:1620, app.js:6281).

claims.claim: §1: The 12-second autosave thumbnail renders the whole scene into a full project-size canvas (about 11 MB per capture at 1080x1920, about 3.35 GB per hour of churn) and never frees its temporary canvases.
claims.evidence: The code path is exactly as described. Each edit schedules a save 600 ms later (js/storage.js:869). save() calls touchCurrent() (js/storage.js:752), and that calls makeThumb() at most once every 12 s while not playing (js/storage.js:2468). makeThumb sets src.width/height = P.width/P.height (js/storage.js:2140) and renders the full scene into it (js/storage.js:2148). renderScene works out its scale as canvas.width / P.width, which is 1 here (js/compositor.js:18746-18747), so the plates are full size too (plateScale at js/compositor.js:3899). The halving chain follows (js/storage.js:2151-2162). makeLayerThumb has the same full-size canvas (js/storage.js:2215-2216). A grep of all js/ at b46b47d3 finds no `.width = 0` or any other canvas release. The app's own comment measures makeThumb at 62 ms under 6x CPU throttle (js/storage.js:2447-2450). Two things are not proved. First, retention: the canvases are local variables and can be garbage-collected, and 3.35 GB/h is turnover that only happens if an edit lands at least every 12 s. Second, the 'resized back and forth' point is weaker on his phone: preview scale is cssW*dpr/P.width*1.25, capped at 1 (js/app.js:564-565), so on a DPR-3 iPhone any preview about 288 CSS px or wider already renders at full size.
claims.user_impact: On his phone, every pause in editing triggers a hidden full-resolution render (a hitch of about 60 ms) and throws away about 11 MB of canvas. iOS Safari counts that canvas memory until it gets round to collecting it, which may be why long sessions go black, but nobody has measured this.
claims.smallest_fix: In makeThumb and makeLayerThumb, size src at 2x the card (width = tw*2, height = th*2); renderScene scales itself from canvas.width. Do one halving, then after toDataURL set width = height = 0 on src and every half canvas.

claims.claim: §2: Compositor scratch pools, _fxScratch and the GL canvases are resized to the current plate on use and never shrunk or released, so roughly 125-170 MB stays resident at 1080x1920 (about 1 GB at 12 MP) for the rest of the session.
claims.evidence: Confirmed that nothing releases them. js/compositor.js declares 17 module-level `const _xxPool = []` arrays (3355, 3507, 4286, 4492, 9135, 9574, 10165, 11581, 11583, 11859, 14605, 14923, 15007, 16680, 17089, 17947, 18411). dspSlot sets four canvases to exactly W x H on every use and has no shrink step (js/compositor.js:10175-10181). _fxScratch only ever grows (js/compositor.js:4690-4694). gl-color resizes its canvas to the last plate (js/gl-color.js:292, :340). A grep of js/ finds no pool reset and no width=0, including on project switch. The thumbnail and export render unstamped canvases at scale 1, and a paused editor only re-renders on the next edit, so between edits these pools sit at FULL project size even when the preview is smaller. Not proved: the MB totals are arithmetic, not measurements. It is also a high-water mark bounded by effect families x nesting depth, not a leak that keeps growing.
claims.user_impact: A project that uses several effects keeps something like 100+ MB of invisible canvases alive for the whole session, even after he goes Home or opens another project. On an iPhone that eats into the headroom before Safari reloads the tab.
claims.smallest_fix: Add one FM.releaseCompositorScratch() in compositor.js that walks the pools, sets width = height = 0 on every canvas and nulls _fxScratch. Call it from the export finally (js/exporter.js around 1633) and from the project-switch media release.

claims.claim: §3a: Every clip that is exported (or reversed, or used by an audio-reactive effect) keeps its full decoded soundtrack on m.audioBuffer until the clip or project is released, about 23 MB per minute of source with no cap. Proposed fix: drop it after export because 'the preview does not use it: it plays the <video>'.
claims.evidence: Retention is confirmed. The exporter decodes every audible clip's whole file into m.audioBuffer (js/exporter.js:561-563). decodeAudio uses `new AudioContext()`, so the device rate (usually 48 kHz), on the whole file (js/media.js:832-842). The only thing that clears it is release (js/media.js:60, also reached from FM.releaseMediaFor). The repo already stopped caching for 'Save as WAV' and 'Remove vocals' for exactly this reason, '~90MB for four minutes of stereo' (js/audio-tools.js:20-29), so the exporter is the odd one out. The fix's reasoning is WRONG, though. The preview does use m.audioBuffer: reversed clips decode it on play and play from it (js/app.js:2629, js/audio-play.js:26, :175), audio-reactive effects read it (js/audio-react.js:43-47), and so does the mono warning (js/inspector.js:2414). Also, null means 'this clip has no audio track' (js/media.js:943), so a fix that sets null would silently mute reversed clips and mislabel clips as silent.
claims.user_impact: After one export of a project with a few long phone videos, hundreds of MB of raw audio stay in memory for the rest of the session, so a second export or further editing on his iPhone is more likely to crash the tab.
claims.smallest_fix: In the exporter's audio mix, note which records had audioBuffer === undefined before it decoded them. After the mix, `delete m.audioBuffer` on those records (back to undefined, never null), skipping reversed clips and clips with audio-reactive links. requestPlay and getBuffer already re-decode on demand.

claims.claim: §3b: Reverse/frame-blend frame caches are budgeted per clip with no global cap: up to 160 MB per clip on a phone, so three reversed or slow-mo clips can hold about 480 MB.
claims.evidence: The per-clip, no-global-cap part is confirmed. The frame count is capped by maxBytes for each record separately (js/frames.js:163), ensureReverseCache passes FM.frameCacheLimits() for each clip (js/app.js:1710), and nothing adds up the total across clips. The number is slightly high for his phone: iPhone Safari has no deviceMemory and is touch, so the budget is 128 MB, not 160 (js/app.js:1690), about 384 MB for three clips. The audit misses the bigger danger next to this. Export throws away the scaled preview cache and rebuilds every reversed or slow-mo clip at FULL source resolution with a fixed maxBytes: 1610612736, which is 1.5 GB PER CLIP and not device-aware (js/exporter.js:1028, :1038-1039). All of them stay alive until the finally (js/exporter.js:1633). The app's own comment says 384 MB of ImageBitmaps is what kills mobile Safari (js/app.js:1678-1680).
claims.user_impact: Exporting on his iPhone a project with a reversed or slow-mo 1080p/4K phone clip can try to hold over 1 GB of decoded frames. That likely gets the tab killed mid-export, so the export just vanishes (likely, not measured).
claims.smallest_fix: In prepareCaches (js/exporter.js), replace the 1.5 GB constant with a device-aware budget shared across the clips being built. For example, on a touch device use FM.frameCacheLimits().maxBytes x 2, divided by the number of clips that need a cache. Long clips then lose frame rate, which effFps already handles, instead of crashing. Divide the preview budget by the number of cached clips the same way.

app-memory.summary: The audit's line numbers are accurate at b46b47d3, and I could not prove any of the four claims wrong. All four mechanisms are real, but each is 'partly'. The memory figures are arithmetic, not measurements, and the thumbnail cost is churn of canvases that can be collected, not proven retention. The audio fix as written would break reversed-clip and audio-reactive sound, because the preview does read m.audioBuffer and null means 'no track'. The frame-cache claim UNDERSTATES the risk: export rebuilds reversed and slow-mo clips at full resolution with a fixed 1.5 GB budget per clip, while the app's own comment says 384 MB kills mobile Safari. That is the most likely real phone crash. The audit is memory-only, so it has no privacy or silent-export claims to test. The ranking I'd give Ezra: (1) the export frame-cache budget, (2) audio kept after export, (3) the full-size 12 s thumbnail, (4) compositor pools never released. I changed nothing, ran nothing, and took no measurements on a device.

claims.claim: F1: The owner's private Notes-pad notes and reminders (scene.project.notes) travel to every guest, Viewers included, and nothing on the Share screens says so.
claims.evidence: js/collab-session.js:31 DENY = ['ofTemplate','ofTemplateRev','ofElement','returnTo','fromTemplate'], so notes is not on it. viewOfProject (:33-43) drops only DENY keys and keys starting with `_`. js/collab-bridge.js:116 view() = viewOfProject(FM.scene.project). C.share builds the host base from that view (js/collab-session.js:1792-1795). H.snapshot sends base.project to every member regardless of role (js/collab-host.js:938-939; sent by sendCopy, js/collab-session.js:777-782). js/collab-path.js:251 lists notes as a synced keyed array. js/notepad.js:14-16 says notes live on the project, and notepad.js has no collab or role check anywhere. styles.css:11145-11157 (body.collab-ro) does not hide the notes button. On a guest, app.js:5613 runs FM.notepad.confirmExport(), so the owner's ticked reminders pop up when the guest exports. The privacy text (js/collab-ui.js:1983-1990) talks only about the network. Exporting a template already strips notes (js/storage.js:3033-3037), which shows the app treats them as private elsewhere. Editors can also edit or delete the owner's notes, because collab-host.js:130 allows any non-comment path for editors.
claims.user_impact: Anything Ezra types in a project's Notes pad (prices, client remarks, to-dos) can be read by every friend he shares that project with, can pop up on their screen as a reminder, and stays in the copy they keep.
claims.smallest_fix: Add 'notes' to DENY in js/collab-session.js:31 (one word). That keeps notes on the owner's device and out of the diff and the hash, but editors would no longer share notes, so Ezra has to choose. The text-only alternative is one line in PRIVACY_FULL: 'Your project notes are shared too.' Either way, add a canary-note test against viewOfProject or the Share text.

claims.claim: F2: 'Viewer: can only watch' is untrue. Viewers can export by default (roExport: true), every guest receives all the raw media, and turning export off does not stop them keeping a copy.
claims.evidence: The label is at js/collab-ui.js:50 ['viewer','Viewer','can only watch'] and appears in the owner's role pickers (:486, :568, :1730) and on the knock card (roleMeans :1161, used near :4096). The default roExport: true is at :360. C.canExport (js/collab-core.js:422) is checked only while a session is live (app.js:5607 requires FM.collab.active). It is worse than the audit says: the guest Leave button (collab-ui.js:3179-3194, then leaveKeeping :3211) calls C.leave with keep (js/collab-session.js:1984), and that calls FM.projects.detachLinked (js/storage.js:2749-2772). detachLinked copies the whole doc and media under a new id and deletes e.collab, so the copy becomes the Viewer's own normal, editable project, and the export gate never applies to it. No role or roExport check exists on that path. The same happens without any tap when the owner stops sharing or removes them (detachEnded, collab-ui.js:4603-4608). The owner's toggle hint does admit 'their copy is on their device either way' (:1819-1820), but the role label still promises 'only watch'.
claims.user_impact: A friend invited 'only to watch' a cut can tap Leave and walk away with the full, editable project and every clip, then export it freely, even if Ezra switched exporting off.
claims.smallest_fix: Change the wording at js/collab-ui.js:50 to 'can watch, and keep a copy' (and match the knock card). If he wants the export switch to mean more, also stop a viewer or commenter from keeping a copy on Leave when roExport === false (call C.leave({keep:false}) on that path). The guest still physically holds the media, so this only changes the buttons.

claims.claim: F5: Media from a peer is decoded with no pixel limit (GIFs are capped only at 64 MP), so a hostile admitted guest can send a small file that exhausts a phone's memory, and because it is stored it decodes again on every reopen.
claims.evidence: Confirmed: FM.loadImageFile (js/media.js:801-807) checks nothing about naturalWidth or naturalHeight. decodeGifAnimation's only guard is W*H > 64e6 (js/media.js:726), and below that it allocates a full W*H*4 Uint8ClampedArray plus a W x H canvas (:729-730), which is about 256 MB + 256 MB at 64 MP, plus a slice() copy for disposal-3 frames. Peer files reach this through writeRecord (js/collab-media.js:1191-1203), which writes the file to IndexedDB BEFORE decoding. The project reopen paths decode it again (js/storage.js:1721, :2120). The only size gate is by bytes (ASK_ABOVE 100 MB, collab-media.js:47, :776), and a solid-colour pixel bomb is tiny in bytes. No other pixel guard exists in js/. Not proven: that it actually crashes. iOS Safari caps a canvas at about 16.7 MP, so the GIF path likely throws and falls back to a still there; the still path relies on lazy browser decode. Only admitted guests who can add layers (owner or editor, collab-host.js:130-131) can send media, and the default link role is Editor (collab-ui.js:360). One extra point: a hostile editor's file lands in the OWNER's original project too.
claims.user_impact: An admitted editor could add one deliberately oversized image or GIF that may freeze or crash the app on phones, possibly every time the shared or owner's project is opened, until the clip is deleted.
claims.smallest_fix: In writeRecord (js/collab-media.js:1191), before writeMedia, read the image's dimensions with FM.loadImageFile(file,{still:true}). If the pixel count is above a budget (e.g. 50 MP), refuse it with a plain message. Also lower the GIF cap at js/media.js:726 from 64e6 to about 16e6. Keep the hard cap off his own imports, because some phones take 200 MP photos.

claims.claim: F4: The owner's internet address reaches anyone holding the link or short code before the owner approves them, even someone he then turns away, and the privacy text does not say so.
claims.evidence: js/collab-signal.js:1533-1543 S.answer accepts the offer, sends the answer (with STUN candidates, js/collab-signal.js:921), waits for the direct connection to open (openedWithin), and runs the handshake, all automatically. Only after that does admitRelay (js/collab-ui.js:2446-2479, 'After the handshake') put up the knock card (`const knock = !member && (room.kind === 'code' || …settings.ask)`, :2479). So ICE has already completed with the owner's device when he taps Decline. The text at js/collab-ui.js:1988 says 'Anyone with your link or short code can see the internet address of each device that joins'. All guest traffic goes through the host (sendToHost), so a link holder sees the owner's address, not other joiners'. The sentence describes the wrong device and leaves out the declined case.
claims.user_impact: Whoever gets hold of Ezra's share link or code (for example a forwarded link) learns his home internet address just by trying to join, even if he never lets them in.
claims.smallest_fix: Reword js/collab-ui.js:1988 to: 'Anyone with your link or short code can see your internet address when they try to join, even if you don't let them in.' Answering only after approval would break one-tap links, so it is not worth doing.

collab-security.summary:
I checked the four audit claims that matter most for real users against the code at b46b47d3. None was proved wrong. I only read code: nothing was run, edited or tested.

- **F1, private notes are shared (confirmed).** The owner's Notes pad notes go to every guest, viewers included. Guests can open the Notes pad, and the owner's ticked reminders pop up on a guest's export. Nothing on the Share screens mentions it.
- **F2, "Viewer: can only watch" (confirmed, and worse than the audit says).** Export is on by default. Even with export switched off, a viewer can tap Leave and keep an unlinked, fully editable copy that exports freely. They also get that copy automatically when the owner stops sharing or removes them.
- **F5, no pixel limit on media from a peer (partly).** There is no size check on images, and GIFs are only capped at 64 MP. The file is saved before it is decoded, so it is decoded again every time the project opens. That it actually crashes a phone is unproven: iOS's canvas limit probably turns the GIF case into a still picture. Only admitted editors can send media, but Editor is the default role for a link.
- **F4, the owner's internet address leaks before approval (confirmed).** His device connects to whoever uses the link or code before the approval card appears, so a person he turns away still gets his address. The privacy sentence about it also names the wrong device.

Smallest fixes:
- **F1:** add 'notes' to DENY in js/collab-session.js:31. Ezra has to decide this, because editors would then lose shared notes.
- **F2:** change the wording at js/collab-ui.js:50, and optionally block keeping a copy on Leave when export is off.
- **F5:** check image size on the peer receive path before saving, and lower the GIF cap.
- **F4:** reword js/collab-ui.js:1988.

The audit's other findings (F3 code strength, F6 AI prompt injection, F7 keys stored in localStorage, F8 Editor as default role) are lower impact, and I did not re-check them.
